cases.title: The starter about AI agents
cases.question: How does Brad ship with AI agents?
cases.answer:
Brad ships with AI agents through a set of rules and checks. Brad's own account says that Brad runs VINDecoded, a profitable vehicle-research product on Android, iOS and the web, as a one-person engineering team where AI agents write most of the code. Of the pull requests, 1,028 of them (83%) came from agent branches in Claude Code and Codex.

Each change is gated by risk. For medium and high risk, the agent writes acceptance criteria as checkable lines, each naming its proof. Acceptance tests are written before the code and locked, so an agent can't pass a test by changing it. When the code is done, a second agent reviews it with fresh context and only read tools, so it can't quietly fix what it finds. Production is guarded too: writing code is cheap and reversible; changing production is not. Most new features reach production turned off, so merging and deploying code doesn't change what customers see.

cases.title: From the essay: features ship dark
cases.question: In Brad’s essay, how do new features reach customers?
cases.answer: New features reach customers in steps, and most ship turned off. Most new features reach production turned off, so merging and deploying code doesn't change what customers see. Turning it on is a separate, deliberate step that takes effect in seconds and can be undone the same way. The steps are: Merged dark. The code ships behind a gate that is off for everyone. Next, on for my account: I switch it on for myself in production through a per-user override. Then on for everyone. One command through the production-task CLI turns the gate on, for example `prod-task shop-ai:on`. Finally, kept with a kill switch. Every live feature keeps a named off switch, such as `prod-task shop-ai:off`, and AGENTS.md lists it beside the feature.
